comments.body:
Fifth plan review 2026-10-18 (BLOCK, 1 move), a substantive one, confirmed on origin/main 21dabcbb2c1:

`list`'s `sort_states` (`src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:57-73`) preserves input order when `--sort` is empty, and ties break ticket_id-ascending with missing values last. The old `session-logs` verb's `recent_session_logs_state` (`reads.py:541-549`) sorts `created_at` descending with a plain stable sort and no tiebreak. So the proposed `list --type=session_log --limit=N` returned the first N rows in input order, not the N newest, and even `--sort=-created` could differ from the library on ties, breaking `tests/interfaces/queries/test_recent_session_logs.py::test_library_cli_mcp_agree` (`lib == cli == mcp` row-for-row at `:99-101`).

Resolution written into the description: the mapping is `list --type=session_log --sort=-created --limit=N` (the hint always includes `--sort=-created --limit=5`); `--limit` applies after `sort_states`; and `recent_session_logs_state` drops its private sort and reuses `sort_states(logs, "-created")[:limit]`, so the library, MCP, and CLI share one ordering rule and the parity test retargets its CLI arm and stays exact. `--limit` without `--sort` is documented as first-N-in-input-order, not newest. New AC pins all of that, including a grep that `recent_session_logs_state` contains no private `.sort(`.

Behavioural note for the implementer: the only observable change for library/MCP callers is the tiebreak on equal `created_at` (now ticket_id ascending instead of input order), which the release note should state.

## Context / Problem
Twelve near-duplicate ticket verbs (`exists`/`format`, `check-ac`/`clarity-check`/`quality-check`, `tag`/`untag`, `get-file-impact`/`get-verify-commands`, `list-descendants`, `session-logs`) each own a route, parser factory, help artifact, and exit-code row while their operation exists on a golden-path verb or fits one flag. Operator decision (2026-09-06): hard cutover, no working aliases; removed spellings fail loudly with a replacement hint via the existing removed-name mechanism, kept and populated. ADR 0100 §8 keeps JSON shapes and exit codes. Mapping, evidence, and overlap ownership: epic toadyish-sulfurous-ovenbird's first comment. Cites: origin/main b97d414b8e2 (re-verified 2026-10-18).
